chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Throwing drafts away, unfinished songs and Fables of Faubus lyrics
summary: Composing frees him from interference; words slow his songs; Faubus words came after the music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Very strange man. Getting back to composing. That to you, of all the three, is the thing that most interests you, and that's been the case --
Well, nobody can bug me when I'm doing that. I can compose when I want to compose.
And, you know, I throw away a whole lot of things until I get what I want to get.
And you go through a whole lot of

If I got a piece -- I got some I haven't even finished. I got one, (singing), take any choice from one to ten, bet you I've got your number, you're still in love with me. I always wanted to finish that one and I never have. Probably because the words don't -- that is it, it's because the words don't come as easily as they came at first. So it held up the music. I almost didn't get through the last on a date, because -- (singing) you say you saw her at the party -- I went on and did it without words. By throwing the words away, I finish a lot of tunes. Seems I (inaudible) words with songs. I try to complete them, but (inaudible).
Yeah. I was just thinking for some reason of the Fables of Faubus, which was, I thought, a very good illustration of how words and music were just so completely correct together. You know?
I didn't write that with words.
Yeah. They seemed to fit right in.
